steps.what: 1. Guard: dealer != null && dealer.IsDead -> zero-damage no-op for every target (CreatureCmd.cs:242-245)
steps.issue: DamageCmd.deal (cmds.py) has no equivalent backstop guard. See guard G5.

steps.what: 2. Guard: empty target list -> no results (CreatureCmd.cs:247-251)
steps.rationale: sim's DamageCmd.deal takes a single Creature, not IEnumerable<Creature>; this batch-emptiness guard has no analogue by construction. See guard N2.

steps.what: 3. Per-target loop guard: originalTarget.IsDead -> skip this target entirely, no hooks fire (CreatureCmd.cs:256-259)
steps.issue: DamageCmd.deal has no target.is_dead guard at entry; a call against an already-dead target would run modify_damage_additive/multiplicative/cap, on_attacked, block absorption, and modify_hp_lost against it (only on_damage_received is guarded, via a separate later check). C# skips the target completely. See guard G5.

steps.what: 4. Hook.ModifyDamage: additive (sum) -> multiplicative (product) -> cap (min); floor at 0 (Hook.cs:1486-1569, 2511-2558)
steps.maps_to: cmds.py step 1-2 (modify_damage_additive/multiplicative gated on is_powered_attack) + step 2 cap (unconditional) + max(0, amount); order and cap-unconditionality match. Two lower-risk nuances recorded separately: the pipeline-level is_powered_attack gate (guard G3) and sequential-chain vs parallel-sum dispatch (guard N3).

steps.what: 5. Event: AfterModifyingDamageAmount(modifiers) (CreatureCmd.cs:262; Hook.cs:694)
steps.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the companion event exists and is dispatched at C#'s position. hooks.modify_damage_additive / modify_damage_multiplicative now take an out-param `modifiers` list and append every listener whose delta was non-zero / factor was not 1 (sts2_rl/hooks.py), and DamageCmd.deal fires hooks.after_modify_damage_amount(modifiers, target) immediately after the two modifier passes and before BeforeDamageReceived -- the slot CreatureCmd.cs:262 occupies. Residue checked and dismissed: the sim applies the cap after the event and does not add a capping listener to `modifiers`, where ModifyDamageInternal does; all three C# AfterModifyingDamageAmount implementers (IntangiblePower, SlowPower, HardToKillPower) have a body of `Flash();` only, so nothing mechanical rides on it. WAS: 'No sim counterpart exists at all -- the modifier hooks returned aggregated values with no companion who-changed-this event.'

steps.what: 6. Event: BeforeDamageReceived, unconditional pre-block/pre-HP/pre-death (CreatureCmd.cs:263; Hook.cs:403-408)
steps.maps_to: cmds.py step 3 on_attacked, correctly positioned before block absorption and gated on amount>0 and MOVE-in-props. The mechanism/position is faithful; the one C# override of this hook (ThornsPower) is wired to a different sim hook entirely -- see guard G1.

steps.what: 7. Block absorption: DamageBlockInternal -- Unblockable => 0 blocked, else min(Block, amount) (CreatureCmd.cs:264-265; Creature.cs:430-435)
steps.maps_to: cmds.py step 4 (`if target.block > 0 and UNBLOCKABLE not in props: absorbed = min(target.block, amount)`) -- identical semantics.

steps.what: 8. Hook.ModifyHpLost, BeforeOsty phase (CreatureCmd.cs:266)
steps.maps_to: cmds.py step 5 modify_hp_lost -- the sim collapses the BeforeOsty/AfterOsty split into one call since Osty redirection is waived (guard N2/step 10).

steps.what: 9. Event: AfterModifyingHpLostBeforeOsty(modifiers) (CreatureCmd.cs:267; Hook.cs:754)
steps.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: hooks.modify_hp_lost carries the out-param `modifiers` list and DamageCmd.deal fires hooks.after_modify_hp_lost(modifiers, target) right after the HP-loss modifier pass. Because Osty redirection is waived, the sim's single modify_hp_lost call covers CreatureCmd.cs:266 and :269 and its single after_modify_hp_lost call covers CreatureCmd.cs:267 and :270 -- the same collapse rationale steps 8 and 11 are faithful under. The only mechanically-meaningful implementer of either variant, BufferPower.cs:29-32, is ported and consumes the notification (sts2_rl/powers.py BufferPower.after_modify_hp_lost); HardenedShellPower, IntangiblePower, TungstenRod, TheBoot and BeatingRemnant all have a body of `Flash();` only. WAS: 'No sim counterpart.'

steps.what: 10. Osty pet-damage redirection: Hook.ModifyUnblockedDamageTarget (CreatureCmd.cs:268; Hook.cs:2048)
steps.rationale: Osty is a pet/companion damage-sharing mechanic; the Ironclad-only, single-player sim has no pet-companion system, so this redirection path is unreachable in scope.

steps.what: 11. Hook.ModifyHpLost, AfterOsty phase, re-run on the (possibly redirected) target (CreatureCmd.cs:269)
steps.maps_to: Collapsed into the single cmds.py step 5 modify_hp_lost call, same rationale as step 8 -- faithful given Osty redirection (step 10) is out of scope.

steps.what: 12. Event: AfterModifyingHpLostAfterOsty(modifiers) (CreatureCmd.cs:270; Hook.cs:769)
steps.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: hooks.after_modify_hp_lost(modifiers, target) is dispatched from DamageCmd.deal after the HP-loss modifier pass, and its docstring names this variant (CreatureCmd.cs:270) as the one it maps to. The listener set is tracked by hooks.modify_hp_lost's out-param, so only listeners that actually changed the amount are notified -- which is what BufferPower.cs:29-32 needs, and the sim's BufferPower is wired to it. WAS: 'No sim counterpart.'

steps.what: 13. Apply: Creature.LoseHpInternal mutates CurrentHp; computes UnblockedDamage/WasTargetKilled/OverkillDamage, WasTargetKilled evaluated before the subtraction (CreatureCmd.cs:271; Creature.cs:445-457)
steps.maps_to: cmds.py step 6 (`target.hp = max(0, target.hp - hp_lost)`) plus step 7's should_die check. The arithmetic-snapshot nature of WasTargetKilled and its downstream interaction with death prevention is recorded separately -- see guard G4.

steps.what: 14. WasBlockBroken = Block<=0 && blockedDamage>0; WasFullyBlocked = !Unblockable && (blockedDamage>0 || Block>0) && unblockedDamage==0 (CreatureCmd.cs:273-274)
steps.maps_to: cmds.py step 4 (`if target.block == 0: hooks.on_block_broken(...)`) -- an exact break counts, matching Block<=0 (Block cannot go negative given the min() absorption). Fires at a different pipeline position than C# -- see guard N5 (no current observable effect).

steps.what: 15. Osty overkill split: second LoseHpInternal against the original target for OverkillDamage when the HP-loss target was redirected (CreatureCmd.cs:275-290)
steps.rationale: Only reachable when Osty redirection (step 10) is active; same pet/companion out-of-scope rationale.

steps.what: 16. Per-result loop: VFX/SFX/history/screen-shake bookkeeping, no gameplay-logic hooks (CreatureCmd.cs:291-369)
steps.rationale: Presentation-only (VFX/SFX/animation triggers); out of scope per the audit's presentation-machinery waiver.

steps.what: 17.1 Second loop, per result: Event AfterBlockBroken if WasBlockBroken, fires AFTER HP loss is applied (CreatureCmd.cs:376-379)
steps.rationale: The sim fires on_block_broken during block absorption (step 7/14 above), before HP loss is applied, rather than after. See guard N5 -- neither currently-ported listener (StunPower via block-break, Hand Drill) reads HP/death state, so this produces no observable difference today.

steps.what: 17.2 Second loop: Event AfterCurrentHpChanged if UnblockedDamage > 0 (CreatureCmd.cs:380-383)
steps.maps_to: cmds.py step 6 (`if hp_lost > 0: ... hooks.on_hp_changed(...)`) -- same guard condition.

steps.what: 17.3 Second loop: dealer.Player.ExtraFields.DamageDealt stat bump (CreatureCmd.cs:384-387)
steps.rationale: Run-level telemetry/stat tracking, not gameplay logic; out of scope.

steps.what: 17.4 Second loop: Event AfterDamageGiven (dealer side), fires whenever combatState != null regardless of WasTargetKilled -- BEFORE the killing-blow-guarded AfterDamageReceived (CreatureCmd.cs:388-391)
steps.issue: cmds.py fires on_damage_dealt (step 9, dealer side) AFTER on_damage_received (step 8, victim side) -- the reverse of C#'s AfterDamageGiven-before-AfterDamageReceived order. Currently dormant: no sim power implements on_damage_dealt yet (grep confirms zero listeners), so no observable divergence exists today, but the pipeline's own dispatch order is inverted from source.

steps.what: 17.5 Second loop: killing-blow guard -- if (!WasTargetKilled || !IsDead) AfterDamageReceived(...) else killedCreatures.Add(...); decided BEFORE Kill()/ShouldDie runs (CreatureCmd.cs:392-399)
steps.issue: The sim resolves should_die (and resets HP to 1 on a prevented death) BEFORE checking target.is_dead for the on_damage_received guard, so a prevented death does NOT skip on_damage_received. C# locks the skip decision to the pre-Kill() snapshot and never revisits it even if death is later prevented. See guard G4.

steps.what: 17.6 Second loop: VFX for fully-blocked hits (CreatureCmd.cs:400-407)

18. Kill(killedCreatures), run after the whole batch's step 17: BeforeDeath -> ShouldDie (early) -> ShouldDieLate (late, e.g. LizardTail) -> death or AfterPreventingDeath; no generic HP reset in Kill() itself (CreatureCmd.cs:409, 489-572; Hook.cs:2229-2249)
steps.maps_to: cmds.py step 7 should_die + on_death/on_death-prevention handling. Core death processing (InvokeDiedEvent-equivalent on_death, corpse-retention via should_remove_from_combat_after_death) matches. Two narrower nuances recorded separately: the single-phase should_die vs C#'s ShouldDie/ShouldDieLate priority split (guard N4, currently inert) and the generic 'reset to 1 HP' fallback replacing each preventer's own AfterPreventingDeath restoration (guard G4).

guards.what: G1: ThornsPower wired to on_damage_received (killing-blow-guarded, post-block) instead of on_attacked/BeforeDamageReceived-equivalent (unconditional, pre-block, pre-death)
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the sim gained a `before_damage_received` dispatcher (sts2_rl/hooks.py), DamageCmd.deal fires it unconditionally after the modifier passes and before block absorption -- CreatureCmd.cs:263's slot, outside the killing-blow skip at CreatureCmd.cs:392 -- and ThornsPower now implements it with the `is_powered_attack(props)` gate its C# counterpart applies. Both recorded consequences are gone: (a) a Thorns bearer reflects off the blow that kills it; (b) unpowered dealer-attributed damage no longer reflects. SEPARATE, NOT PART OF THIS GAP (raised in this pass): the sim's reflect calls DamageCmd.deal with no `dealer`, where ThornsPower.cs passes base.Owner as the dealer of the reflected hit. WAS: Thorns hung on on_damage_received (post-block, killing-blow-guarded) with no props gate.

guards.what: G2: no AfterModifyingXxx(modifiers) companion-event machinery anywhere in the sim's damage-modifier hooks
guards.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THREE of the 13 AfterModifying* variants now exist and are dispatched at C#'s positions: HpLost (hooks.after_modify_hp_lost, built for BufferPower), DamageAmount (hooks.after_modify_damage_amount, fired from DamageCmd.deal) and BlockAmount (hooks.after_modify_block_amount, fired from BlockCmd.apply, mirroring CreatureCmd.cs:646). Each is backed by a real out-param `modifiers` list in the corresponding modifier hook, so only listeners that actually changed the value are notified. WHAT REMAINS: the other ten variants Hook.cs declares (Hook.cs:649-829) have no sim counterpart -- CardPlayCount, CardRewardOptions, EnergyGain, GoldGained, HandDraw, OrbPassiveTriggerCount, PowerAmountGiven, PowerAmountReceived, Rewards, and the RestSite pair. PowerAmountGiven / PowerAmountReceived remain this guard's sharpest edge: they sit on the Unsettling Lamp seam and are separately recorded as power_cmd's guard G4. Two further residues inside the three that landed: the sim's damage cap does not contribute to `modifiers` (all three C# AfterModifyingDamageAmount implementers are Flash-only, so this is inert), and after_modify_block_amount fires AFTER the block has been added where CreatureCmd.cs:646 fires it BEFORE GainBlockInternal (Vambrace, the one ported listener, reads neither block nor HP). ORIGINAL: no AfterModifying* companion-event machinery existed anywhere in the sim's modifier hooks.

guards.what: G3: pipeline-level is_powered_attack(props) gate around the entire modify_damage_additive/multiplicative dispatch, vs C#'s always-call-every-listener-and-self-gate architecture
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the pipeline-level gate is gone. DamageCmd.deal now calls hooks.modify_damage_additive and modify_damage_multiplicative for EVERY damage and passes `props` through to each listener, matching ModifyDamageInternal (Hook.cs:2515-2538), which has no props gate and leaves the IsPoweredAttack test to each implementation; BlockCmd.apply does the same on the block side against Hook.ModifyBlock (Hook.cs:1310-1340). Strength, Vulnerable, Weak, Dexterity, Frail and Fasten self-gate on is_powered_attack / is_powered_card_or_monster_move_block; Vambrace, Pael's Legion and Unmovable self-gate on is_card_or_monster_move (Move ALONE) as their C# counterparts do; SurroundedPower deliberately does not gate, in either codebase, so the Kaiser Crab back-attack multiplier now survives an Unpowered hit as it does in the game. SEPARATE FALLOUT, NOT THIS GAP: DiamondDiademPower (sts2_rl/powers.py) still relies on the removed pipeline gate -- its comment says so -- where DiamondDiademPower.cs:27-30 self-gates on IsPoweredAttack; that is a power-tier defect raised in this pass's surprises. WAS: cmds.py skipped the whole modifier dispatch when is_powered_attack(props) was false.

guards.what: G4: killing-blow post-damage-event skip decision is recomputed after death-prevention resolves in the sim, but is a locked pre-Kill() snapshot in C#
guards.issue: NARROWED AND RE-GROUNDED 2026-07-27: the divergence stands, but its mechanism has changed and the old description is no longer accurate. The 'reset HP to 1' step is GONE -- _resolve_death's prevented-death arm (sts2_rl/cmds.py) now leaves the creature dead at 0 HP and fires on_death(target, True) then after_preventing_death(preventer, target), mirroring CreatureCmd.cs:565-570. What survives is the ORDERING: DamageCmd.deal still resolves death (step 8) BEFORE it evaluates `if not target.is_dead` for on_damage_received (step 9), where C# locks the AfterDamageReceived decision to the pre-Kill() WasTargetKilled/IsDead snapshot at CreatureCmd.cs:392 and only calls Kill() afterwards, at CreatureCmd.cs:409. A preventer that heals therefore still un-deads the creature before the guard is read: LizardTail's after_preventing_death heals to 50% max HP (sts2_rl/relics/lizard_tail.py), Creature.is_dead becomes False, and on_damage_received fires. The recorded witness is unchanged in substance -- LizardTail + CentennialPuzzle: C#'s killing-blow-guarded CentennialPuzzle.AfterDamageReceived does not draw on a Tail-prevented lethal hit; the sim's centennial_puzzle.on_damage_received does, and draws 3. Fairy in a Bottle (sts2_rl/potions.py should_die) reaches the same state by the same route. ORIGINAL: the sim floored a prevented death at 1 HP inside DamageCmd.deal and then tested is_dead.

guards.what: G5: DamageCmd.deal has no dealer-is-dead or target-is-dead entry-guard backstop
guards.issue: C#'s CreatureCmd.Damage refuses to process any hit at all from an already-dead dealer (CreatureCmd.cs:242-245, spec step 1) and skips any already-dead target in its per-target loop (CreatureCmd.cs:256-259, spec step 3), both as hard backstops independent of caller discipline. The sim's DamageCmd.deal has neither guard; it relies entirely on call sites to check is_dead between hits of a multi-hit/multi-target attack (e.g. sts2_rl/monsters/base.py:114-117 `_execute_attack`, sts2_rl/cards/whirlwind.py:43-49, both of which currently do this correctly on spot-check). No concrete failure is demonstrated -- this records the structural absence of the pipeline-level backstop, not a proven exploit.

guards.what: G6: dealer-side AfterDamageGiven fires before victim-side AfterDamageReceived in C#; the sim's on_damage_dealt fires after on_damage_received
guards.issue: CreatureCmd.cs:388-395 fires AfterDamageGiven (dealer side, unconditional) before the killing-blow-guarded AfterDamageReceived (victim side). cmds.py's DamageCmd.deal fires on_damage_received (step 8) before on_damage_dealt (step 9) -- the reverse order. Currently dormant: no sim power implements on_damage_dealt yet, so no observable divergence exists with current content, but the pipeline's dispatch order for these two event families is inverted from source and would matter for a dealer-side power/relic that needs to observe pre-victim-reaction state, or vice versa.

guards.what: N1: sim-only should_allow_hitting pre-check has no single C# analogue inside CreatureCmd.Damage
guards.rationale: C# excludes unhittable/reviving creatures upstream, via IsAlive-based target filtering in AttackCommand.GetPossibleTargets (AttackCommand.cs:544-546) plus real-death semantics for reviving Decimillipede-style segments, rather than a dedicated hook inside CreatureCmd.Damage itself. The sim's should_allow_hitting hook (used only by MockRevivePower/ReattachPower-family reviving-segment logic, sts2_rl/powers.py:1572-1575, 2354-2357, 3372-3375) re-architects this as an explicit pipeline predicate. Net effect is equivalent for the currently-ported content (Decimillipede); documented so a future audit doesn't mistake it for an unmapped C# hook.

guards.what: N2: DamageCmd.deal takes a single Creature per call; CreatureCmd.Damage batches IEnumerable<Creature> and defers all targets' step-17/18 events until every target in the call has resolved blocking/HP-loss
guards.rationale: The sim's callers (card code, Monster._execute_attack) loop over multiple simultaneous targets themselves, each a fully independent DamageCmd.deal call including its own Kill() processing, rather than the pipeline batching them. For a C# attack that hits several creatures at once, every target's AfterDamageGiven/AfterDamageReceived-or-skip resolves before ANY of them is actually Kill()'d; in the sim, the first target's entire pipeline (including death processing) completes before the second target's begins. No concretely broken current interaction was found (the one candidate, Decimillipede's ReattachPower 'are all other segments dead' check, is evaluated on a segment's own later turn, well after any same-turn AOE has already fully resolved in both architectures), but this is a real structural difference. Cross-reference: primarily the concern of the creature_card_cmds seam (Task 7), which owns how cards orchestrate multi-target attacks; recorded here because it originates in DamageCmd.deal's own signature.

guards.what: N3 (LIVE): additive/multiplicative dispatch is a parallel sum/product in the sim vs a sequential running-value chain in C# -- RAISED from deliberate-divergence to gap in the Task 9 fix pass
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: hooks.modify_damage_multiplicative is now a CHAIN, not a product -- it folds each listener's factor into the running amount and returns the new amount, exactly as ModifyDamageInternal does (`num *= item2.ModifyDamageMultiplicative(...)`, Hook.cs:2515-2538) -- and DamageCmd.deal applies the returned value directly. The block twin, hooks.modify_block_multiplicative, was changed the same way against Hook.ModifyBlock (Hook.cs:1310-1340), which closes the site creature_card_cmds step 13 carried. The recorded witness now agrees: Shrink (x0.7) plus Vulnerable (x1.5) on a 20-damage powered attack gives 20*1.5 = 30, 30*0.7 = 21. The strict xfail that pinned this (test_multiplicative_damage_modifiers_chain_sequentially) is gone from test/test_hook_order.py and the test passes. The additive family still hands every listener the same pre-step base rather than the running total, which is exactly equal over integers and was already settled on the merits. WAS: the sim multiplied every factor together in float and applied the product once, giving 20 where the game gives 21.

guards.what: N4: C#'s ShouldDie (early) / ShouldDieLate (late) two-phase death-prevention priority collapsed to a single flat pass in the sim
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the sim gained real hook PHASES. HookSystem._each runs a complete listener pass per suffix in the order _very_early, _early, plain, _late (sts2_rl/hooks.py), so hooks.should_die now makes a full plain pass before any Late one -- the shape Hook.ShouldDie has at Hook.cs:2229-2249. The two contending listeners are wired to their real phases: FairyInABottle implements the plain `should_die` (sts2_rl/potions.py) and LizardTail implements `should_die_late` (sts2_rl/relics/lizard_tail.py, matching LizardTail.cs being the source's only ShouldDieLate implementer), so a held Fairy is now always spent before the Tail. WAS: hooks.should_die was one flat pass and the sim spent whichever listener happened to be registered first.

guards.what: N5: on_block_broken fires during block absorption (before HP loss is applied) in the sim; AfterBlockBroken fires after HP loss is applied in C#
guards.rationale: cmds.py step 4 fires on_block_broken immediately when block hits exactly 0 during absorption; CreatureCmd.cs:376-379 fires AfterBlockBroken later, in the second per-result loop, after LoseHpInternal has already mutated CurrentHp (step 13). Both fire unconditionally regardless of whether the same hit also kills the target. Currently ported listeners (StunPower-on-block-break in sts2_rl/powers.py:2293-2300, Hand Drill in sts2_rl/relics/hand_drill.py:21-29) read neither HP nor death state, so no observable difference exists today.
